doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: New York and the WDR Big Band
title: Public radio funding and commissioned music
summary: German broadcast tax funds the WDR band, which commissions new music from writers such as Mendoza, Abene and Mintzer.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Is the ensemble supported by the State — national funding, that kind of thing.

Yes. All the public broadcasting in Germany is supported by a broadcast tax that every citizen pays or every household pays. So we are in the State of North Rhine-Westphalia and the citizens of North Rhine-Westphalia support the West German radio, which is Westdeutscher Rundfunk West German radio, that’s what we’re called. So yes, they make it possible.
Nice. I wish we would learn from that.

Yes it really is amazing the system and the appreciation that it creates here for this music and I think often about how much music we have played over the years that would have never — wouldn’t exist if it weren’t for this because this music is always or almost always commissioned for the band. So this music wouldn’t exist if somebody here in the West German radio wouldn’t take money and say to Vince Mendoza or to Michael Abene or to Bob Mintzer or to Jim McNeely or whoever, say please write a program of Michel LeGrand’s music arranged for the big band with this and that soloist and being part of this creation is quite something.
